judges.persona: first-time player and Space Apps judge

quiz.where: A stop called 'Light-toned patch', about 55 m from the habitat (stop 1 on the map). The Site tab had told me the crew was going to Cheyava Falls, 785 m away, so I'm not sure.
quiz.safe: Probably yes. The Route panel says steepest slope 13 degrees, which is in the 0-15 'walkable' band of the legend, 'Over 15 m' is 0, and it says 'Tightest limit: time, 21 min to spare'. Nothing on this screen says GO or NO-GO, though.
quiz.how_long: Unclear. The Route panel shows '3 min Planned out', but the Time slider says 30 min. My guess is about 3 to 4 minutes out and back, inside a 30 minute budget.
quiz.layer_meaning: Terrain layer, slope from the HiRISE elevation model. Uncoloured ground is 0-15 degrees and walkable, orange is 15-20 degrees and needs caution at standard risk, red is over 20 degrees and no-go. The white lines are contours every 5 m.

findings.where: Site title 'Cheyava Falls' (785 m from the habitat) vs Route title 'First sortie', with stop 1 'Light-toned patch' at 55 m
findings.problem: The Site tab sells Cheyava Falls as the destination. The Route tab then plans a 0.05 km walk to an unnamed patch nearby, and Cheyava Falls never shows up on the route map or in the Stops list.
findings.why: A first-time viewer gets 'where are we going' wrong or contradicts themselves. The whole pitch, a walk to the biosignature rock, disappears on the most important screen.
findings.fix: Either make the default route end at Cheyava Falls, or label stop 1 'Warm-up stop, 55 m (Cheyava Falls is 785 m, next sortie)'. Also draw Cheyava Falls as a pin on the Route map.

findings.where: Map drag and scroll zoom (film-drag, film-zoom)
findings.problem: Panning and zooming update at about 15 fps. The longest gaps are 257 ms (drag) and 270 ms (zoom), and most frame-to-frame gaps run about 270-290 ms. Pins jump instead of gliding, and after the drag the route has left the view.
findings.why: Gaps over 200 ms make the map feel stuck. A judge dragging the map live will read it as broken or underpowered.
findings.fix: Pan and zoom with a CSS or GPU transform on the cached layer canvas, and re-render the layer only when input stops. Clamp the pan so the route stays in view, and keep 'Fit route' visible.

findings.where: Route panel top right: '3 min Planned out' next to the Mission needs slider 'Time 30 min'
findings.problem: 'Planned out' is jargon, and two different time numbers sit on one screen. Nowhere does it say 'EVA takes X min' or show a GO or NO-GO verdict. The verdict only appears later, on the Suit tab.
findings.why: A judge can't answer 'how long' or 'is it safe' at a glance on the screen the team calls most important.
findings.fix: Lead the Route panel with one line, 'GO · 4 min walk · 26 of 30 min to spare', coloured green, amber or red. Rename 'Planned out' to 'Walk time' and the slider to 'Time budget'.

findings.where: 'Back at the habitat': '+285 min oxygen margin' vs Decision 'Tightest limit: time, 21 min to spare' and the time bar '21 spare'
findings.problem: One panel shows a margin of 285 minutes and another shows 21 minutes, with no explanation of how they differ.
findings.why: Conflicting safety numbers make the model look made up. The walkback margin is the core idea of the product.
findings.fix: Show the binding margin as the big number ('21 min to spare, time is the limit'). Move oxygen to a secondary line such as 'oxygen would last 285 min more'.

findings.where: Map layer buttons, Terrain hover thumbnail
findings.problem: Hovering a layer button opens a large thumbnail preview over the Stops list and the 'Map layer' heading. In the quiz screenshot it hides stop 1's name.
findings.why: It looks like a rendering glitch and hides the destination.
findings.fix: Drop the hover thumbnail, or open it to the right of the button over the map, with a short delay, and close it on click.

findings.where: 3D Z-2 suit model in the centre
findings.problem: The suit texture is patchy, with white and grey blotches that look like missing texture or z-fighting.
findings.why: It looks unfinished on the go or no-go screen judges see right before Begin EVA.
findings.fix: Fix the material or normals (double-sided, correct UVs) or use a clean flat-shaded material.

demo_as_is.why: The Site tab promises Cheyava Falls and the Route tab walks somewhere else, 55 m away. Pan and zoom stall for 250-290 ms per frame. The mission table has no plain GO or NO-GO or EVA duration. Fix the destination mismatch and the map motion and it would look professional. The visual design and data labelling are already strong.

quiz.where: From the Habitat (stop 0) to a stop called 'Light-toned patch' (stop 1), about 0.05 km away to the north-west. The screen title is 'First sortie'. Nothing on this screen names Cheyava Falls.
quiz.safe: Probably yes, but I have to infer it because the Route screen shows no go or no-go. The evidence is 'Over 15° m: 0', 'Steepest slope 13°' (under the 15° caution band), 'No radio %: 0', 'Tightest limit: time, 21 min to spare', and a line that stays clear of the orange and red patches. 'Begin EVA' is enabled.
quiz.how_long: '3 min Planned out', against a 30 min time budget with 21 min to spare. I cannot tell from this screen whether 3 min is the outbound leg, the round trip, or includes work at the stop.
quiz.layer_meaning: Terrain is on. It shows slope derived from the HiRISE elevation model: no tint is 0-15° (walkable), orange is 15-20° (caution at standard risk), red is over 20° (no-go). The legend says white lines are contours every 5 m, and that slope 'decides where the route bends'. A second legend also uses a white line for Perseverance's drives, so I cannot tell which white lines are which.

findings.where: Site title 'Cheyava Falls' with '785 m from the habitat', against the Route title 'First sortie' and the Stops panel 'Light-toned patch, 55 m'
findings.problem: The Site tab briefs the crew on Cheyava Falls, 785 m away. The Route tab then plans a 55 m walk to a different place, 'Light-toned patch', on a map 150 m across that does not contain Cheyava Falls. Nothing explains the switch.
findings.why: A judge asked 'where is the crew going' answers Cheyava Falls after the Site tab and is wrong. A planner cannot sign a go or no-go when the briefed target and the routed target differ.
findings.fix: Either make Cheyava Falls the default goal, or add a line on the Site tab and in the Route title such as 'First sortie: 55 m shakedown walk to the light-toned patch. Cheyava Falls is 785 m, sortie 2'. Show both targets on the Site map.

findings.where: The map during drag and scroll zoom, and the first paint after clicking Route
findings.problem: Drag delivers 77 frames in 4.9 s (about 16 fps) with a longest gap of 257 ms. Zoom delivers 75 frames in 3.4 s with a 270 ms gap. The Route tab takes 390 ms to first paint, then a 220 ms gap.
findings.why: All three pass the 200 ms mark where the map feels stuck. This is the screen the demo depends on, and a judge who drags the map will see it stutter.
findings.fix: During pan and zoom, move the already rendered map and overlay as one transformed bitmap and redraw the layer only when the gesture ends. Keep the route map mounted behind the Site tab so the tab switch paints in one frame.

findings.where: Route panel '3 min Planned out', and the Suit panel time bar '3 out, 2 min of it work · 1 back · 21 spare · 5 reserve'
findings.problem: 'Planned out' does not say whether 3 min is outbound, round trip, or includes work. The Suit bar implies the EVA is 4 min (3 out including 2 of work, 1 back), yet the headline still says '3 min out'. Distance reads 0.05 km in one panel and 55 m in another, and 'Climb +0 m' sits next to 'Steepest slope 13°'.
findings.why: I could not answer 'how long will the EVA take' with confidence from the Route screen. Total duration is the first number a planner needs.
findings.fix: Lead with one total: 'EVA 4 min: 1 walk out, 2 work, 1 back'. Show distance in metres at this scale (55 m one way, 110 m round trip). Show climb to one decimal, or as gain and loss.

findings.where: 'Begin EVA' on the Route tab, and the Decision panel 'Go' on the Suit tab
findings.problem: The Route tab has no go or no-go state, and its 'Begin EVA' button lets the crew leave without opening Hazards or Suit. On the Suit tab, 'Go' is green while the text under it says 'A radiation alert is expected during the walk'. The dust storm, also ticked for this run, is not mentioned in the Decision panel at all.
findings.why: A go that states an expected radiation alert and omits an enabled dust storm reads as a decision that ignores its own hazards. A planner would challenge it in the first minute.
findings.fix: Put a compact status strip on the Route tab ('Go · slope ok · radio ok · 21 min spare'). Change the Route button to 'Next: hazards', and leave 'Begin EVA' on the Suit tab only. In the Decision panel, list each enabled hazard with its planned response, and label the state 'Go, with 2 drill events' so the scripted alerts read as a drill.

findings.where: Terrain preview thumbnail over the Stops panel, and the two legends at the bottom of the map
findings.problem: The Terrain preview popover covers the stop list, the stop distance and the 'Rover' toggle, and it does not match the map's colours (pink bands against the map's orange and red). Contours and Perseverance's drives both use a white line in their legends, so the white lines on the map are ambiguous. The '0-15° walkable' swatch is an empty box.
findings.why: The layer that 'decides where the route bends' is the one whose lines I cannot attribute, and switching it on hides the list of where the crew is going.
findings.fix: Anchor the preview above the buttons without covering Stops, or drop it once the layer is on. Draw rover drives in a distinct colour or dashed style, and thin the contours. Label the walkable swatch 'no tint'.

findings.where: Conditions outlook row, the 'Back at the habitat' panel, the suit figure, and the Dust storm card
findings.problem: Several numbers lack context. '+285 min oxygen margin' sits beside a 30 min time limit and a 3 min walk with no statement of which one governs. 'Space weather 224 min warning' reads like an active warning. 'Sky exposure 0.95 mean · 0.95 at its most sheltered' has no unit and shows the route offers no shelter without saying so. 'Opacity climbs to 8' on the Dust storm card has no symbol or baseline, while the Suit tab uses 'τ 0.45'. The suit model also shows grey patches that look like missing texture.
findings.why: These are the numbers a strict reviewer reads first. The patchy suit looks like a rendering fault in the centre of the last screen before launch.
findings.fix: Write 'Oxygen is not the limit: 285 min beyond reserve. Time is: 21 min spare'. Rename to 'Solar event lead time: 224 min (2017 event)'. Write 'Sky view 0.95 of open sky everywhere: no shelter on this route'. Write 'τ rises from 0.45 to 8'. Fix or relight the suit textures.

demo_as_is.why: The content is honest about sources and the terrain legend is readable, but three things would fail in front of a judge. The Site tab promises Cheyava Falls and the route goes to a different stop 55 m away. The map stutters at 257 to 270 ms gaps when dragged or zoomed. The EVA duration is stated as '3 min out' without a clear total. The filmstrip named film-layer-toggle.png also shows a Risk change from Standard to Cautious with the layer staying on Image, so I could not judge the layer toggle motion from it. Fix the destination mismatch, the map motion and the duration headline before showing it.

quiz.where: Light-toned patch, stop 1 on the map, 55 m from the habitat. The page title says only "First sortie", and nothing on this screen names Cheyava Falls.
quiz.safe: Probably yes, but I had to infer it. Nothing on the Route screen says go or no-go. I read it from "Tightest limit: time, 21 min to spare", from the steepest slope of 13 degrees being under the 15 degree walkable limit, and from "Over 15° m: 0".
quiz.how_long: 3 min planned out to the stop (Route panel), inside a 30 min time budget. The screen gives no total round-trip EVA time.
quiz.layer_meaning: Terrain shows slope from the HiRISE elevation model. Clear means 0 to 15 degrees, walkable. Orange or amber means 15 to 20 degrees, caution at standard risk. Red means over 20 degrees, no-go. The white lines are contours every 5 m.

findings.where: Map canvas during drag and scroll zoom
findings.problem: The map hitches on every drag and zoom. The drag strip has gaps up to 257 ms, and the map jumps from one position to another with nothing in between, as at t=1449 and t=3053. Zoom has gaps up to 270 ms. Tab switch (220 ms) and layer or risk change (187 ms, with Begin EVA dimmed while "Planning...") are also past the 50 ms hitch limit.
findings.why: At over 200 ms per frame the map feels stuck. On the most important screen of the demo, a judge reads it as broken before reading any data.
findings.fix: Pan and zoom with a CSS or GPU transform on an already-rendered layer, and re-render or re-plan only on pointerup or after a debounce. Move the route planner off the main thread to a worker so input frames stay under 16 ms.

findings.where: Site title "Cheyava Falls", 785 m; Route stop 1 "Light-toned patch", 55 m
findings.problem: The Site tab sells Cheyava Falls 785 m away, but the planned route goes to a different place 55 m away and takes 3 min. The Route screen never names Cheyava Falls, and the page title switches to "First sortie".
findings.why: Anyone asked where the crew is going gets it wrong or has to guess. The product thesis is the walk to the biosignature rock, and the route doesn't go there.
findings.fix: Make Cheyava Falls the default destination, or say it on the Route screen. For example, set the title to "First sortie to Light-toned patch, a 55 m shakedown before Cheyava Falls" and show Cheyava Falls as a greyed later stop on the map.

findings.where: "Terrain" hover preview over the Stops and Map layer panels
findings.problem: The layer preview thumbnail stays open after the click. It covers stop 1's name and the "Map layer" label and leaves a stray outline box at about x=250, y=630.
findings.why: It looks like a rendering bug and hides the stop list, the only text record of where the route goes.
findings.fix: Close the preview on click and on pointerleave. Better, anchor it above the button row so it never covers the Stops panel.

findings.where: Route panel "21 min to spare"; Suit "+285 min oxygen margin", 99 % rings; no verdict on Route
findings.problem: Safety is split across screens and the numbers disagree. Route has no go or no-go at all. Suit shows "Go" with 21 min spare, then a green +285 min margin and 99 % rings, all in the same alert green.
findings.why: Two different margin numbers in green make a designer stop and ask which one limits the walk, and the walkback margin is the core mechanic.
findings.fix: Put one go or no-go chip with the limiting margin at the top of the Route stats panel, for example "Go · 21 min walkback margin (time)". On Suit, make 21 min the hero number and move the 285 min oxygen figure below it in neutral grey as secondary detail.

findings.where: Hazard severity chips "Warning", "Can happen in this run" checkboxes, and the "3 out" bar segment on Suit
findings.problem: The main-action orange #ff6a2b also fills the warning chips, the three checkboxes and the time bars, alongside the orange "Next: suit check" button. The Route profiles tabs add off-palette purple and yellow-green underlines.
findings.why: The orange button stops being the one obvious action, and alert colours lose their meaning when decorative colours look like them.
findings.fix: Use amber and red for warning chips. Make checkboxes neutral white on dark. Draw the spend bars in neutral greys with green for spare. Reserve orange for the single CTA. Mark the alternative routes with cyan dash patterns or grey instead of purple and yellow.

findings.where: Map caption "North up · 150 m across", SIM, DERIVED and DATA chips, Route profiles footnote, Stops goal text
findings.problem: Secondary text is under the 11 px floor and in low-contrast grey. The jargon "Fastest: the planner as before" and the contradictory "+0 m Climb" next to a 13° slope also need cleanup.
findings.why: At 1366x768 on a projector, judges can't read it, and the odd copy looks unfinished.
findings.fix: Raise captions and chips to 11 px or larger at higher contrast. Rewrite the footnote as "Fastest: shortest walk time for this slope and rock". Show the climb as net and gross, or with a decimal.

demo_as_is.why: The map hitches on every drag and zoom with gaps over 250 ms, the terrain preview sticks over the Stops panel, and the route goes to a 55 m patch instead of Cheyava Falls with no go or no-go on the Route screen. Judges would see a stuck map and misread both the destination and the safety call.

quiz_facts.safe: route.decision is pending on the Route step; route.totals.status nominal; Suit step shows Go
quiz_facts.how_long: about 4 min: 3 min out including 2 min of work, 1 min back (Suit step time bar)
quiz_facts.layer_meaning: Terrain: slope 0-15 walkable, 15-20 caution at standard risk, over 20 no-go, contours every 5 m

quiz_result: where 3/3 right (j1 unsure after the Site tab). safe 3/3 inferred 'probably yes' with no verdict on screen. how_long 0/3 gave the total of about 4 min: blocker. layer_meaning 3/3 right; j2 could not tell contours from rover drives (both white).

consensus.issue: map hitches on drag and zoom (257 to 290 ms gaps)
Site briefs Cheyava Falls at 785 m, Route walks 55 m to a light-toned patch with no explanation
no go or no-go and no total EVA time on the Route step; 'Planned out' is ambiguous
two margins disagree: 21 min spare (time) vs +285 min oxygen
consensus.action: issue for keiwv (same issue as the go or no-go)

consensus.issue: layer hover preview stays open after the click and covers the Stops panel
